title: OSHA construction personal protective equipment practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction PPE practice questions on 29 CFR 1926 Subpart E. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: An employee already owns adequate protective equipment and the employer allows him to use it on the job. What does 1926.95(d)(6) say about reimbursing him for it?

options.A: The employer is not required to reimburse the employee for that equipment
options.B: The employer must reimburse the full purchase price
options.C: The employer must reimburse half of the purchase price
options.D: The employer must reimburse the employee when the project ends

questions.explanation: Where an employee provides adequate protective equipment he or she owns, "the employer may allow the employee to use it and is not required to reimburse the employee for that equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer does not have to pay for non-specialty steel-toe boots on what condition?

options.A: The employee has worked there less than 90 days
options.B: The boots cost less than $100
options.C: The employer permits the boots to be worn off the job site
options.D: The boots were bought before the project began

questions.explanation: The employer is not required to pay for non-specialty safety-toe protective footwear (including steel-toe boots) and non-specialty prescription safety eyewear, "provided that the employer permits such items to be worn off the job-site."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The employer provides metatarsal guards, but an employee asks to wear his own boots with built-in metatarsal protection instead, and the employer allows it. What does 1926.95(d)(3) say about paying for those boots?

options.A: The employer must reimburse the full cost of the boots
options.B: The employer is not required to reimburse the employee for the shoes or boots
options.C: The employer must pay for both the boots and the metatarsal guards
options.D: The employer must pay the employee the value of the metatarsal guards

questions.explanation: When the employer provides metatarsal guards and allows the employee, at his or her request, to use shoes or boots with built-in metatarsal protection, "the employer is not required to reimburse the employee for the shoes or boots."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Another OSHA standard specifies whether or not the employer must pay for a specific piece of equipment. Which payment provisions prevail, according to the note to 1926.95(d)?

options.A: Those in 1926.95(d), in every case
options.B: Whichever provisions cost the employer less
options.C: Whichever provisions the employee chooses
options.D: The payment provisions of that other standard

questions.explanation: The note to 1926.95(d) says that when the provisions of another OSHA standard specify whether or not the employer must pay for specific equipment, "the payment provisions of that standard shall prevail."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.95(a), in what condition must protective equipment be provided, used and maintained wherever hazards make it necessary?

options.A: In a sanitary and reliable condition
options.B: In its original packaging until the first use
options.C: In a condition certified by OSHA each year
options.D: In a locked storage area between shifts

questions.explanation: Protective equipment "shall be provided, used, and maintained in a sanitary and reliable condition" wherever it is necessary by reason of hazards capable of causing injury or impairment.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.95(c), PPE must be selected to ensure what?

options.A: That it is the lowest-cost option
options.B: That it properly fits each affected employee
options.C: That it matches company colors
options.D: That it is made in the United States

questions.explanation: Employers must ensure all PPE "is of safe design and construction for the work to be performed" and "is selected to ensure that it properly fits each affected employee."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.96, safety-toe footwear for employees must meet the requirements of which American National Standard?

options.A: ANSI/ISEA Z87.1-2010
options.C: Z41.1-1967, for Men's Safety-Toe Footwear
options.D: Federal Specification QQ-P-416

questions.explanation: Safety-toe footwear for employees "shall meet the requirements and specifications in American National Standard for Men's Safety-Toe Footwear, Z41.1-1967."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.96, Occupational foot protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Head protection for employees exposed to high-voltage electric shock and burns must also meet which part of the named ANSI Z89.1 standards?

options.A: Section 9.7 ("Electrical Insulation")
options.B: Section 1.1 ("Scope")
options.C: The annex on color coding
options.D: Nothing more than the general requirements

questions.explanation: For employees exposed to high-voltage electric shock and burns, head protection must also meet "Section 9.7 ("Electrical Insulation")" of one of the consensus standards listed in 1926.100(b)(1).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.100, Head protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.101(a), when must ear protective devices be provided and used?

options.A: Only when an employee asks for them
options.B: Wherever it is not feasible to reduce the noise levels or duration of exposures to those in Table D-2
options.C: On every construction site, whatever the noise level
options.D: Only during pile driving

questions.explanation: "Wherever it is not feasible to reduce the noise levels or duration of exposures to those specified in Table D-2, Permissible Noise Exposures, in § 1926.52, ear protective devices shall be provided and used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.101, Hearing protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Who must fit or determine ear protective devices that are inserted in the ear?

options.A: The employee alone
options.B: Any coworker
options.C: The equipment vendor's sales staff
options.D: Competent persons, individually for each user

questions.explanation: "Ear protective devices inserted in the ear shall be fitted or determined individually by competent persons."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.101, Hearing protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What marking does 1926.102(a)(4) require on eye and face PPE?

options.A: A distinct marking to facilitate identification of the manufacturer
options.B: The name of the employee who wears it
options.C: The date it was purchased
options.D: The number of the last OSHA inspection

questions.explanation: "Eye and face PPE shall be distinctly marked to facilitate identification of the manufacturer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.102, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee who wears prescription glasses does work with eye hazards. Which option does 1926.102 allow?

options.A: Wearing the prescription glasses alone
options.B: Skipping eye protection for tasks under one hour
options.C: Wearing eye protection that fits over the prescription lenses without disturbing either lens's position
options.D: Wearing contact lenses instead of eye protection

questions.explanation: The employee must wear eye protection "that incorporates the prescription in its design, or wears eye protection that can be worn over the prescription lenses without disturbing the proper position of the prescription lenses or the protective lenses."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.102, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1926.102 say about using a welding filter shade more dense than the one listed in its Table E-1?

options.A: It is prohibited
options.B: It requires OSHA approval
options.C: It may be used to suit the individual's needs
options.D: It is allowed only for soldering

questions.explanation: Table E-1 "shall be used as a guide" for selecting shade numbers, and "Shades more dense than those listed may be used to suit the individual's needs."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.102, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where does 1926.103 say the respiratory protection requirements for construction work are set out?
questions.explanation: The note in 1926.103 says the requirements for construction work "are identical to those set forth at 29 CFR 1910.134 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.103, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.104(a), for what purpose may lifelines, safety belts and lanyards be used?

options.A: Hoisting tools and materials
options.B: Towing equipment around the site
options.C: Any purpose, if they are rated above 5,400 pounds
options.D: Only for employee safeguarding

questions.explanation: "Lifelines, safety belts, and lanyards shall be used only for employee safeguarding."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.104, Safety belts, lifelines, and lanyards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1926.104(e) require of safety belt and lanyard hardware?

options.A: It may be cast aluminum if it is anodized
options.B: It may be any material rated for 1,000 pounds
options.C: It must be drop forged or pressed steel, cadmium plated, with a smooth surface free of sharp edges
options.D: It must be molded plastic with a non-slip coating

questions.explanation: "All safety belt and lanyard hardware shall be drop forged or pressed steel, cadmium plated in accordance with type 1, Class B plating specified in Federal Specification QQ-P-416. Surface shall be smooth and free of sharp edges."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.104, Safety belts, lifelines, and lanyards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where safety net protection is required by Part 1926, when may the operations it protects be undertaken?

options.A: As soon as the net has been delivered to the site
options.B: Once at least half of the net has been hung
options.C: After the first day of work on the level above
options.D: Only after the net is in place and has been tested

questions.explanation: Where safety net protection is required by this part, "operations shall not be undertaken until the net is in place and has been tested."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.105, Safety nets (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.105(e), what must be used to fasten a safety net to its supports?

options.A: Forged steel safety hooks or shackles
options.B: Nylon cable ties
options.C: Knots tied in the edge rope by the crew
options.D: Wire rope clips only

questions.explanation: "Forged steel safety hooks or shackles shall be used to fasten the net to its supports."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.105, Safety nets (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A bridge crew works over a river where the danger of drowning exists. Besides life jackets or buoyant work vests and ring buoys, what boat requirement does 1926.106 set?

options.A: One motorboat for every 10 employees
options.B: A skiff kept within one mile of the site
options.C: No boat, because ring buoys are enough
options.D: At least one lifesaving skiff immediately available

questions.explanation: "At least one lifesaving skiff shall be immediately available at locations where employees are working over or adjacent to water."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.106, Working over or near water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection before use finds a defect in a buoyant work vest that would alter its buoyancy. What does 1926.106(b) say about that vest?

options.A: It may be used if it is taped over
options.B: It shall not be used
options.C: It may be used only near the shore
options.D: It may be used only by a strong swimmer

questions.explanation: Vests and life preservers are inspected for defects which would alter their strength or buoyancy, and "Defective units shall not be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.106, Working over or near water (as of Nov 3, 2026)
